summary: Redwood AE and SE walked Avalon Insurance through the SIG questionnaire and mapped key controls. Main concerns: data residency for EU customers, KMS/encryption ownership, SSO/SAML integration and RBAC, and audit log retention. Redwood to provide SOC 2 artifacts, SSO metadata, and sample logs; follow-up scheduled.
transcript:
[00:00] Avery (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Avery from Redwood Inference. Ravi the SE is here with me. Hi team.
[00:06] Mark (CISO): Hi Avery, hi Ravi. Mark from Avalon Insurance. We have Priya, Daniel and Leah on the call as well.
[00:12] Priya (Security Manager): Morning. Thanks for the invite. We sent you the SIG earlier today, appreciate walking through.
[00:18] Avery: Yep yep, we got it. Goal for today is to walk the SIG/CAIQ items you flagged as high priority and call out where we can provide evidence. We'll try to hit encryption, SSO/RBAC, audit logs, and data residency.
[00:26] Ravi (SE): I'll jump in on technical parts, show what docs and exports we can provide. Quick note, transcription may have small errs, apologies if names get munged.
[00:35] Daniel (Procurement): We also need to confirm timelines — SOC 2 report and any contracts.
[00:40] Avery: Sure. Quick status: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II in place; latest report is from 2025 and we have 2026 attestation in progress. We can share the full SOC 2 report and the mapping to SIG controls.
[00:50] Mark: When you say in progress, is that Type II for the service? We need Type II for the platform used in production.
[00:55] Avery: Yes, current public is Type II for our hosted platform through 2025. The 2026 audit is underway; we'll share what we can, and the SOC 2 bridge letter if helpful.
[01:02] Priya: Ok. For evidence we prefer PDF plus the CAIQ cell-level mapping. Can you provide that?
[01:07] Avery: Absolutely, we'll attach a CAIQ-mapped spreadsheet and a zip of evidence artifacts where permissible. Sensitive docs will be redacted per our policy.
[01:14] Leah (IT Ops): On SSO — do you support SAML 2.0 and SCIM provisioning? We need SSO with IDP (Okta) and automated user provisioning.
[01:20] Ravi: Yes, we support SAML 2.0 and SCIM. Provisioning is supported via SCIM v2; we can provide a sample SCIM manifest and our SAML metadata for Okta.
[01:27] Priya: Do you support Just-in-Time provisioning or full SCIM?
[01:30] Ravi: We support full SCIM provisioning; JIT also works but SCIM is preferred for enterprise. Role mapping is configurable — you can map groups from Okta to our RBAC roles (admin/editor/viewer).
[01:39] Mark: And RBAC — can you do attribute-based access? We want least privilege and split between dev and prod access.
[01:44] Ravi: We have role-based with fine-grained resource scoping. Attribute-based rules can be approximated via group claims in SAML or SCIM attributes. We don't currently support full ABAC policy language like OPA out of the box, but it's on the roadmap.
[01:54] Daniel: For the SIG question on multi-tenant data separation, can you explain how data is isolated for dedicated vs hosted?
[02:00] Avery: Sure. Hosted: logical tenancy with strong encryption and namespace isolation; dedicated: can be dedicated capacity with tenant-level isolation including VPC peering options. For on-prem/private we provide customer-managed infra. We'll flag which SIG controls apply to each deployment model.
[02:12] Priya: Data residency — we have EU-only customer data. Can we guarantee EU-only processing?
[02:17] Ravi: We have regional routing and EU regions for data processing. For full EU-only guarantees, we recommend Redwood Dedicated in EU or Redwood Private deployed in your VPC. Hosted accounts can be restricted to EU regions; we can document the controls and routing policy.
[02:31] Leah: Is data at rest encrypted? Where are keys stored?
[02:34] Avery: Yes — encryption at rest by default. Keys are managed in our KMS. For hosted we use a managed KMS and rotate keys regularly; customers on Dedicated/Private can use customer-managed KMS/HSM. We support bring-your-own-key via KMS integrations.
[02:48] Mark: Is there support for HSM-backed keys?
[02:50] Ravi: Yes, for enterprise customers we can integrate with HSM-backed KMS providers — AWS CloudHSM, Azure Key Vault with HSM, or customer HSM on-prem. We'll include a KB article showing the integration steps.
[02:59] Priya: Audit logs — how granular are they and how long do you retain them? Our policies require 365 days of immutable logs.
[03:06] Avery: Default retention is 90 days on hosted; enterprise plans offer configurable retention up to multiple years. We can export immutable logs to your S3/GCS bucket with object lock for compliance. We'll provide sample export format and retention options.
[03:20] Ravi: The audit logs include authentication events, API calls (model name, route, request metadata), admin changes and deployments. Personal data in logs is minimized; we can redact prompt content on export if needed.
[03:33] Mark: Redaction is important. We need the ability to redact PII from logs, and also to produce a forensics export if needed.
[03:39] Ravi: Understood. We have log filters and can produce an export that excludes prompt text. For forensics we provide a secured bundle with chain-of-custody metadata. We'll show sample redaction parameters.
[03:50] Priya: On the SIG there's a question re: threat modeling and pen test cadence. What's your approach?
[03:55] Avery: We run annual third-party pen tests and internal periodic scans. We also have a continuous vulnerability management program. We'll send the latest pentest summary and remediation timelines.
[04:03] Daniel: For legal, we need DPA and standard clauses for data processing. Is your DPA template available?
[04:07] Avery: Yes, we'll share our standard DPA and security addendum. It includes data processing terms and subprocessor list.
[04:13] Mark: Encryption in transit — TLS version?
[04:15] Ravi: We enforce TLS 1.2+ with modern ciphers; mutual TLS supported for private endpoints.
[04:20] Priya: Regarding incident response / notification windows, what SLA do you commit to?
[04:24] Avery: We have an incident response playbook and notify customers within 72 hours for suspected breaches; for critical incidents we notify as soon as possible and provide periodic updates. For Dedicated customers with SLA, we can arrange tighter notification SLAs.
[04:36] Leah: For the CAIQ evidence packs, will you provide Control IDs mapped to SOC 2 assertions?
[04:40] Avery: Yes, we'll provide a CAIQ spreadsheet with SOC 2 mapping, and where we cannot provide evidence (e.g., customer-managed configs) we'll annotate it.
[04:48] Mark: Some SIG fields ask for diagram of network segmentation — can we get an architecture diagram?
[04:52] Ravi: We'll attach a simplified network diagram and an annotated version for Dedicated and Hosted.
[04:56] Priya: Any concerns about HIPAA? We have a line of business with PHI — do you support HIPAA BAAs?
[05:02] Avery: We do offer BAAs for customers that need HIPAA coverage on dedicated/private options; hosted accounts require additional review. We'll include the BAA template and discuss scope.
[05:12] Daniel: Pricing/contract impact for Dedicated vs Hosted — high level now is fine.
[05:16] Avery: We'll follow up with a dedicated commercial note; primary goal today is security evidence.
[05:19] Priya: A few SIG-specific items: change management evidence, privileged access reviews, and encryption key rotation records — do you have historical proof?
[05:25] Ravi: Yes, we retain change logs and privileged access reviews for admins; key rotation logs are retained. We'll provide redacted examples demonstrating timestamps and approvers.
[05:34] Mark: Are you ISO 27001 certified?
[05:36] Avery: We are in the process — ISO scope has been defined and implementation is underway; not yet certified. We'll be transparent about current state in the mapping doc.
[05:44] Priya: For the SIG automated checks, can you mark answers as 'in scope' vs 'customer responsibility'? We need clarity so we can sign off internally.
[05:50] Avery: Absolutely — our CAIQ will mark ownership: Redwood, Customer, or Shared and include required customer actions for shared controls.
[05:58] Ravi: I'll also prepare a short video showing SCIM provisioning and SAML metadata import — might help the Ops team.
[06:04] Leah: That would be helpful.
[06:06] Avery: Ok next steps recap: we'll send SOC2 PDF + CAIQ mapping, SAML metadata and SCIM docs, sample audit logs with redaction options, network diagram, pentest summary, and DPA/BAA template. Schedule a follow-up in one week.
[06:20] Mark: Sounds good. Anything else?
[06:23] Daniel: No, thanks.
[06:24] Priya: Thanks everyone.
[06:26] Avery: Thanks, we'll follow up.
[45:00] -- meeting end --

Notes: Transcription contains some minor name mislabels typical of automated transcripts. References made to internal KB articles (will be shared as links in follow-up).
